public_rationale: Zitron gave his own estimate of about $61 billion in total generative AI revenue, including hyperscalers and neoclouds. He named no period and did not say whether he meant realized revenue or run rate. Public data offers pieces but no total. OpenAI reportedly earned about $4.3 billion in the first half of 2025 and targeted $13 billion for the year. Microsoft reported a $13 billion AI run rate. Alphabet and Amazon do not break out generative AI revenue. Lab and cloud revenue also overlap, because labs pay the clouds. With no credible industry-wide figure on a clear basis, the estimate can be neither confirmed nor refuted.
limitations: The result depends on period and basis choices the speaker did not make.
Company-level figures come mostly from press reports, not filings.

our_interpretation: Plain reading: the speaker gives his own estimate that all generative AI revenue earned across the industry, including hyperscalers and neoclouds and presumably model companies, adds up to about $61 billion.
He gives no period. The closest reading is recent annual revenue as of the post, so roughly calendar 2025 up to the post date. That choice is flagged.
He does not say whether this means realized revenue or annualized run rate. The claim can only be checked against a credible industry-wide total on a stated basis, and none exists.
criteria.support_condition: A credible, sourced industry-wide total of generative AI revenue for the period around the post, covering hyperscalers, neoclouds and model companies, that comes to roughly $61 billion (within about 25%).
criteria.contradiction_condition: A credible industry-wide total for the same period and basis that is far from $61 billion (for example, under about $45 billion or over about $80 billion).
